MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which number is written in words as "nine thousand and ten"? (1 mark)
   A. 910
   B. 90,100
   C. 9,010
   D. 9,100

2. How many factors does 50 have? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 7
   C. 5
   D. 8

3. Which list shows all the factors of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   B. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   C. 1, 2, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   D. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15

4. What is the next number in the pattern 3, 7, 11, 15, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 18
   B. 23
   C. 20
   D. 19

5. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 6,478 + 2,355? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 0
   D. 3

6. Work out 5,008 − 2,999. (1 mark)
   A. 2,019
   B. 3,991
   C. 2,009
   D. 1,909

7. Which sum checks that 5,432 − 2,718 = 2,714? (1 mark)
   A. 2,714 − 2,718
   B. 5,432 + 2,714
   C. 5,432 + 2,718
   D. 2,714 + 2,718

8. Work out 7,000 − 3,456. (1 mark)
   A. 4,456
   B. 3,554
   C. 3,544
   D. 3,444

9. A tank held 8,000 litres of water. The school used 3,450 litres. How many litres are left? (1 mark)
   A. 5,450 litres
   B. 4,550 litres
   C. 4,650 litres
   D. 4,540 litres

10. What is the next number in the pattern 2, 6, 18, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 24
   B. 54
   C. 36
   D. 20

11. What is 18 × 50? (1 mark)
   A. 68
   B. 9,000
   C. 90
   D. 900

12. 50 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 8 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 7
   C. 8
   D. 6

13. Change 31/10 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/10
   B. 4 1/10
   C. 3 2/10
   D. 1 3/10

14. In the fraction 3/5, what does the numerator 3 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many of the equal parts are taken
   B. The size of each part in centimetres
   C. How many equal parts the whole has
   D. The number of wholes

15. What is 1/3 of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 16
   C. 24
   D. 8

16. Change 25/6 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5 1/6
   B. 1 4/6
   C. 4 1/6
   D. 4 2/6

17. Write 0.75 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 7/5
   B. 75/100
   C. 75/10
   D. 75/1000

18. Which is greater, 0.6 or 0.06? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be told
   B. They are equal
   C. 0.6
   D. 0.06

19. A farmer plants seedlings 50 cm apart. How long is a row with 9 gaps between the seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. 450 m
   B. 4 m 50 cm
   C. 4 m 5 cm
   D. 5 m 50 cm

20. A rope 5 m 25 cm long is cut into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 50 cm
   B. 5 m 22 cm
   C. 1 m 75 cm
   D. 1 m 85 cm

21. A fence uses 5 pieces of wire, each 3 m 50 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 17 m 40 cm
   B. 3 m 55 cm
   C. 18 m 50 cm
   D. 17 m 50 cm

22. A pencil starts at the 5 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 10 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 15 cm
   B. 10 cm
   C. 5 cm
   D. 6 cm

23. A rectangle is made of 5 rows with 8 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 45 square units
   B. 13 square units
   C. 40 square units
   D. 26 square units

24. A garden bed marked in 1 m squares has 9 rows and 4 columns. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 36 square metres
   B. 49 square metres
   C. 26 square metres
   D. 13 square metres

25. A rectangle is made of 10 rows with 10 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 20 square units
   C. 110 square units
   D. 100 square units

26. A cuboid is 10 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 100 blocks
   B. 110 blocks
   C. 17 blocks
   D. 50 blocks

27. What should you check first before using a beam balance? (1 mark)
   A. That it has a 1 kg mass in each pan
   B. That both pans are full
   C. That it is near a window
   D. That the beam is level when both pans are empty

28. The price Ksh 12.50 shows how many whole shillings and how many cents? (1 mark)
   A. 125 shillings and no cents
   B. 12 shillings and 5 cents
   C. 12 shillings and 50 cents
   D. 1 shilling and 250 cents

29. 75 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1.75
   B. Ksh 0.75
   C. Ksh 0.07
   D. Ksh 7.50

30. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 1,200, Ksh 2,350 and Ksh 875. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 4,425
   B. Ksh 4,325
   C. Ksh 4,525
   D. Ksh 4,435

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks and cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Work out both volumes and say which is greater. (4 marks)

32. Sort these fractions into proper, improper and mixed: 3/8, 11/5, 2 1/2, 9/9, 7/10. (4 marks)

33. A learner says that a half turn is the same as two quarter turns. Is the learner right? Explain. (2 marks)

34. A group of five tallies and 3 more tally marks show which number? Explain how you count. (2 marks)

35. Write 0.8 and 0.37 as fractions. (2 marks)

36. Explain why we should change lengths to centimetres before adding 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

37. A farmer joins 4 pieces of wire, each measuring 2 m 30 cm, to make one long wire. Find the length of the long wire. (3 marks)

38. Round 47, 342 and 995 to the nearest ten. (3 marks)

39. List four materials you could use to collect and record data about the types of vehicles that pass the school gate. (4 marks)

40. A gate opens through a half turn from its closed position. Describe the angle between the gate and the wall in its closed position. (2 marks)

41. A school timetable shows assembly from 8:00 a.m. to 8:20 a.m. and mathematics from 8:20 a.m. to 9:10 a.m. Find how long each lasts and the total time. (4 marks)

42. A classroom floor is covered with 15 rows of 10 tiles. How many tiles are used? If 6 tiles are broken and must be replaced, how many tiles are unbroken? (4 marks)

43. Write 4 3/8 as an improper fraction. (3 marks)

44. Add 3,568 and 2,276 and say how many times you regrouped. (3 marks)

45. A farmer packs 84 mangoes equally into 4 baskets. How many mangoes are in each basket? Then he picks 3 more mangoes. Can he share all 87 mangoes equally among the 4 baskets? Explain. (5 marks)

46. Explain why 2a + 3b cannot be written as 5ab. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 9,010
   nine thousand and ten: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 9,010.

2. A — 6
   The factors of 50 are 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50. There are 6 of them.

3. B — 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 30. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30.

4. D — 19
   The rule is add 4. 15 + 4 = 19.

5. B — 2
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 6,478 + 2,355 needs 2 regroupings.

6. C — 2,009
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 5,008 − 2,999 = 2,009. Check: 2,009 + 2,999 = 5,008.

7. D — 2,714 + 2,718
   Addition undoes subtraction. 2,714 + 2,718 = 5,432, the starting number.

8. C — 3,544
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,000 − 3,456 = 3,544. Check: 3,544 + 3,456 = 7,000.

9. B — 4,550 litres
   Subtract 8,000 − 3,450 = 4,550. Check by adding: 4,550 + 3,450 = 8,000.

10. B — 54
   The rule is multiply by 3. 18 × 3 = 54.

11. D — 900
   18 × 5 = 90, then × 10 gives 900.

12. B — 7
   50 ÷ 8 = 6 remainder 2. The 2 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 7 trays are needed.

13. A — 3 1/10
   31 ÷ 10 = 3 remainder 1. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 1/10, so 31/10 = 3 1/10.

14. A — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 3/5 it says that 3 parts are taken.

15. D — 8
   24 ÷ 3 = 8 and 8 × 1 = 8. So 1/3 of 24 is 8.

16. C — 4 1/6
   25 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 1. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 1/6, so 25/6 = 4 1/6.

17. B — 75/100
   The last digit of 0.75 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.75 = 75/100.

18. C — 0.6
   Compare the tenths first. 0.6 is greater than 0.06.

19. B — 4 m 50 cm
   9 × 50 = 450 cm = 4 m 50 cm.

20. C — 1 m 75 cm
   525 ÷ 3 = 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm.

21. D — 17 m 50 cm
   350 × 5 = 1750 cm = 17 m 50 cm.

22. C — 5 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 10 − 5 = 5 cm.

23. C — 40 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 5 × 8 = 40 square units.

24. A — 36 square metres
   9 × 4 = 36 square metres.

25. D — 100 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.

26. A — 100 blocks
   One layer has 10 × 5 = 50 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 50 × 2 = 100 blocks.

27. D — That the beam is level when both pans are empty
   The beam must be level when empty for the measurement to be correct.

28. C — 12 shillings and 50 cents
   The digits after the decimal point show the cents.

29. B — Ksh 0.75
   75 ÷ 100 = 0 remainder 75, so it is Ksh 0.75.

30. A — Ksh 4,425
   Add the three costs: 1,200 + 2,350 + 875 = 4,425.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: A = 40 blocks, B = 60 blocks. B is greater by 20 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for the volumes, 1 mark for the comparison, 1 mark for the difference.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Proper: 3/8 and 7/10. Improper: 11/5 and 9/9. Mixed: 2 1/2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group and 1 mark for placing all five correctly.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Yes. A half is made of two quarters, so two quarter turns make one half turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for yes, 1 mark for the reason.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8. Count the group of five as 5, then add 3 more: 5 + 3 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 8 and 1 mark for the explanation.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8/10 and 37/100
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fraction.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: When both lengths are in centimetres we can add them like ordinary numbers: 345 + 280 = 625 cm. This avoids mistakes with regrouping 100 cm into 1 m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using one unit, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for reference to regrouping.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 230 × 4 = 920 cm (2 marks); 920 cm = 9 m 20 cm (1 mark).

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 50, 340 and 1,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rounding. 995 goes up to 1,000 because the ones digit is 5.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: a pencil, an exercise book or paper, a ruler for drawing a table, a clipboard or hard book, a watch or clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible material.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: They make a straight line, which is two right angles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a straight line and 1 mark for two right angles.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Assembly 20 minutes, mathematics 50 minutes, total 70 minutes (1 hour 10 minutes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duration, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 1 h 10 min.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: 150 tiles; 144 tiles unbroken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 15 × 10, 1 mark for 150, 1 mark for 150 − 6, 1 mark for 144.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 35/8
   Working / marking points: 4 × 8 = 32 (1 mark); 32 + 3 = 35 (1 mark); denominator stays 8 (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,844. You regrouped twice (ones to tens, tens to hundreds).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct sum, 1 mark for the carries, 1 mark for saying twice.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: 21 mangoes in each basket. 87 ÷ 4 = 21 remainder 3, so he cannot share all 87 equally; 3 will be left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 21, 2 marks for 87 ÷ 4 = 21 R 3 with working, 1 mark for answering no, 1 mark for the explanation.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: a and b are different, so 2a and 3b are not like terms and cannot be joined.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for unlike terms and 1 mark for the reason.
